Subject: Baseline hosted rate + discounting approach for scale

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating hosted inference for a new conversational agent and need a clear baseline so procurement can model costs. Two asks: a) a simple baseline rate table for hosted API (per 1M tokens) across a few scale buckets (10M, 50M, 200M, 500M+ tokens/month) and b) a short explanation of how Redwood treats burst vs committed usage (carryover, soft-commit options, and what triggers overage pricing).

A few details that matter for our modeling:
- Expected token mix will be generation-heavy (approx 70% output tokens) with average request context ~800 tokens.
- We currently expect to land in the US region, latency SLOs are standard (<300ms tail).
- We're interested in both 12-month and 36-month amortization examples.

If you can share an indicative matrix and any caveats (are there separate charges for KV/cache or batching assumptions?), that would be great. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through.

Thanks,
Lydia
Director of ML Ops
Skyport AI

Lydia —

Attaching an indicative workbook (pricing_matrix_q2.xlsx). Key highlights below so you have a quick reference without opening the file: 

Indicative hosted API list (USD per 1M tokens, post any standard PLG discounts):
- 0 — 10M / month: $120 per 1M tokens
- 10M — 50M / month: $95 per 1M tokens
- 50M — 200M / month: $65 per 1M tokens
- 200M+ / month: $45 per 1M tokens

Notes on the table and mechanics:
- These are hosted (multi-tenant) rates; Dedicated or Private deployments have different unit economics (we can run those separately).
- The figures assume the token distribution you flagged (70% generation). If generation ratio is lower, effective per-1M pricing improves by ~6-12% due to fewer output tokens.
- Batching & KV-cache assumptions: workbook assumes moderate batching and prefix cache behavior (we model ~8% cost savings at scale from batching + cache). If you have strong reuse patterns we can model higher cache uplift.

Soft-commit / carryover options (examples):
- Soft-commit A: 30% of committed volume billed upfront as a refundable credit; unused committed units carry over for 2 months; overage billed at next tier rate.
- Soft-commit B: 50% commitment with staged discounts and a 3-month carryover window; includes a 10% guaranteed burst buffer (subject to capacity).
- Overage protection: for both options we offer a capped overage multiplier (1.25x the nearest listed tier) and a monthly SLA credit schedule if sustained latency or downtime exceeds the agreed SLOs.

Amortization examples (in workbook):
- 12-month sample: spreads any upfront commit credit evenly over 12 months; shown as effective $/1M after amortization.
- 36-month sample: gives larger effective discount assuming commitment stability and provides an example of how we amortize any one-time onboarding/ingestion credits.

Next steps: if these ranges look reasonable, tell us your preferred commit band (10M, 50M, 200M, 500M) and we’ll produce a signed term sheet + SOW. I'm available for a pricing walkthrough Tuesday or Wednesday next week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

1) When you say "moderate batching and prefix cache behavior" — does the workbook assume any particular prompt/prefix reuse rate? Our workload reuses a fairly large system prompt and common context for ~40% of requests.
2) The soft-commit mechanics: if we pick Soft-commit A (30% up front) and hit a month where usage is 3x committed level due to a marketing spike, what happens day-of? Is there an automatic burst allotment or would we immediately pay overage at the multiplier you mentioned?
3) On SLA credits — can you point to the draft schedule you use (months of downtime => % credit) so procurement can evaluate exposure?

If you can answer these in a short note that’s great; otherwise we can take the walkthrough.

Lydia

Subject: Re: Indicative scale-tier matrix + soft-commit options (pricing_matrix_q2.xlsx attached)

Hi Lydia — quick answers inline: 

1) Prompt/prefix reuse: the workbook default assumes ~10–15% high-reuse prefix traffic. Given your note of ~40% reuse we expect incremental cost savings of ~6–9% in the mid-tier bands; we can re-run the workbook with your exact telemetry to show the adjusted effective $/1M.

2) Burst behavior on Soft-commit A: you get an implicit burst buffer equal to 10% of committed capacity for immediate spikes. Anything beyond that is billed as overage at the nearest tier rate with the overage multiplier capped at 1.25x, but we also offer a one-time emergency burst add-on (pre-approved capacity) for additional headroom if needed. We can put a clause in the term sheet to allow pre-authorized emergency bursts for marketing spikes.

3) SLA credits: we use a standard monthly SLA credit schedule (examples in sample_msa_template.pdf attached). High level: 99.9–99.5% uptime => no credit; 99.5–99.0% => 5% monthly credit; 99.0–95.0% => 15% monthly credit; <95% => higher remediation and escalation paths. Legal can tailor for enterprise.

Next steps: we'll update the workbook with a 40% reuse assumption and produce a 1-page term sheet showing the effective amortized price for 12m and 36m under both Soft-commit A and B. Can you confirm a preferred commit band to model (10M / 50M / 200M / 500M)? Also, would you like a 60-minute walkthrough next Tuesday (Apr 20) at 10am PT?

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing this for procurement.

Best,
Priya
